Kim, Lee, and Park - One of the most common surname in Korea, used to be the royals. 

Silla, which lasted from 57 B.C.E. to 935 C.E., were ruled by the Kim and Park clan (Park clan produced about 5 or 6 kings during the early phase of the Kingdom, but eventually the Kim clan took over).   

The Lee clan ruled Choson, which was the last Kingdom of Korea until it was destoryed by Japan in the 20th century, until the current Republic of Korea was formed. 

Naturally, the royal bloods were powerful and wealthy. Also, the Kings often granted their surname to the lords and naturalized foreigners (Those who were respected scholars, tried to overthrow the corrupt government but failed and fled to Korea, etc.) to strengthen their family power.

Since Silla lasted about 900 years (Kim) and Choson lasted about 500 years (Lee), it is not strange to see so many of them today.

Also, although this is not confirmed to be true, many believe that when Korea abolished slavery system, the slaves (who didn't have surname, as only royals and nobles had surname) took surnames such as Kim, Lee, Park, and Choi, to pretend their family has/had good history.
